A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LRAgent work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and can be matched despite additions, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original HotpotQA and ScienceQA experiments, cache-similarity measurements, runtime and memory evaluations, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds activation-similarity, MATH debate-agent, mixed-training, and context-overlap experiments.

M1.justification: BaseShared, shared-A BaseLRShared, and Flash-LoRA-Attention retain the same cache decomposition, role assignment, and attention computation, including Algorithm 1. The additional experiments test the existing method.

E1.justification: v2 adds MATH generation/critic debate agents for cache-similarity evaluation (A.5) and partial/no-overlap context scenarios (D.6). HotpotQA and ScienceQA remain the end-to-end task benchmarks; the MATH addition reports representation diagnostics, not mathematical-answer accuracy.

E2.justification: The main Non-Shared, FullShared, and DroidSpeak comparisons remain unchanged. However, the rank ablation changes from Non-Shared, BaseShared, and BaseLRShared in v1 Table 17 to BaseShared alone in v2 Table 19, removing comparisons within that experiment.

E3.justification: Added protocols include shuffled joint HotpotQA/ScienceQA training, 128 MATH contexts of 2k tokens, ranks 1 and 2, and overlap ratios from 0% to 100% at a fixed 33.7k-token trajectory length. Existing main-experiment settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands supplementary analysis with input-activation similarity (A.2), different agent-role structure on MATH (A.5), mixed-domain training (C.3), and context-overlap sensitivity (D.6). The rank study adds lower ranks and ScienceQA coverage but removes Non-Shared and BaseLRShared rank analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report seed 42, 20 evaluation iterations per benchmark level, and identical standard deviations in Appendix D.5 (v1 Table 18; v2 Table 20). No new uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance test is reported.

E6.justification: Substantial supplementary findings are added: activation similarity averaging 0.9762, MATH full/base/LR similarities of 0.9553/0.9766/0.9620, mixed-training accuracies, partial-overlap throughput, and revised rank results. Main Tables 1–5 remain numerically unchanged. Attribution in new Table 9 is unclear: its BaseLRShared caption accompanies separate-training scores of 31.15/76.58, which match BaseShared in Table 3.

T1.justification: The cosine-similarity assumptions and derivation in v1 A.2/v2 A.3, and the attention derivations in Appendix B, remain unchanged. The added discussion characterizes orthogonality as a practical approximation without revising the formal assumptions or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and central claims: cache decomposition, the two sharing schemes, Flash-LoRA-Attention, near-non-shared accuracy, and efficiency approaching fully shared caching.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations based on relative rather than absolute cache similarity, expected behavior under heterogeneous roles, and diminishing benefits with reduced overlap. It also discusses limited trajectory availability and the applicability restriction when deployed weights cannot be changed to shared-A.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 documents shuffled joint training and reuse of the existing hyperparameters. Section 4.1 removes the FastChat Engine implementation attribution. Existing hardware, training details, prompts, and code-access information otherwise remain; the reformatted repository link has the same target.

R1.justification: v2 adds Stoica et al. (2025) and Luong and Chen (2026) to support the LoRA-alignment interpretation, and Subramaniam et al. (2025) for the debate-agent setting. The principal novelty positioning against earlier cache-sharing methods is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, shared-A background, and experimental setup receive limited rewriting. New appendix subsections and acknowledgments are added, and correspondence/publication text is updated. The overall organization and main narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 7 and Tables 7, 9, and 21, restructures the rank table, and redraws Figure 6 from a two-by-two arrangement into one row without changing its results. Figure 2 changes column placement, with further local reflow and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added activation, role-heterogeneity, and overlap analyses strengthen support for the cache-sharing rationale and clarify operating limits. The net gain is limited: the central evidence is unchanged, the rank comparison is narrowed, and mixed-training Table 9 has unresolved method attribution because its control values match BaseShared in Table 3 despite its BaseLRShared caption.
